premises.claim: Every k-dimensional orthogonal marginal of a cap-one product density has density cap at most 2^(k/2)
premises.scope_used: k=1 for c^T X and k=2 for P^T X and R^T Y

partner_result_actually_applied.application: If an outer physical Schur pivot d has a residual with the new rank-two-cross-plus-scalar-slope certificate M=3*2^(5/6)(||c|| Delta)^(-1/3), then ||p_Q||inf<=2*sqrt(3*2^(5/6))*|d|^(-1/2)(||c|| Delta)^(-1/6).

quantitative_result: For Q=aZ^2+bZ+2Z c^T X+F(X)+G(Y)+2X^TBY with mutually independent original-coordinate scalar/banks, rank(B)=2, Delta=sigma1(B)sigma2(B), the law has a continuous C0 density with ||p_Q||inf<=3*2^(5/6)(||c|| Delta)^(-1/3). A diffuse target family has spectrum {-sqrt2,-1,1,sqrt2}, arbitrarily small physical pair determinants, and the uniform bound <5.346.
unresolved_implication: From bare s_3(A)>=1, force or aggregate this one-sided scalar-slope plus rank-two-cross packet, or route its failure to existing hub/ridge/grouped/near-coloop exits. The theorem does not cover simultaneous scalar coupling into both sides of the cross bank, and arbitrary extra spectrum remains a global compiler debt.
